questions.q: A 7-year-old boy presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Culture yields Staphylococcus aureus. What is the most appropriate first-line topical treatment for this localized condition?
questions.exp: Mupirocin (Bactroban) is the first-line topical antibiotic for localized non-bullous impetigo caused by S. aureus or S. pyogenes. It inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase. Retapamulin is an alternative.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with hypopigmented scaly patches on the trunk that become more noticeable after sun exposure. KOH preparation shows short curved hyphae with round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis (tinea) versicolor is caused by Malassezia species (predominantly M. globosa). The KOH appearance of short hyphae and spores is classically called 'spaghetti and meatballs.' Under Wood's lamp it shows golden-yellow fluorescence.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents 6 days after unprotected intercourse with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the labia majora, dysuria, and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. The most appropriate first-line treatment is:
opts: Acyclovir 400 mg thrice daily for 7–10 days
Benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: This is primary genital herpes (usually HSV-2). First-line oral antivirals — acyclovir 400 mg TDS or 200 mg 5×/day, valacyclovir 1 g BD, or famciclovir 250 mg TDS — for 7–10 days reduce duration and severity.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with an indurated, painless ulcer on the glans penis. VDRL is reactive 1:16; TPHA confirms infection. The drug of choice is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre) is treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose. Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days is used when penicillin is contraindicated. The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction may follow treatment.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man from a leprosy-endemic area presents with a single well-defined hypopigmented anesthetic patch on the forearm. Slit-skin smear is negative. Histopathology shows epithelioid granulomas with giant cells reaching the basal layer, surrounded by dense lymphocytes. Ridley-Jopling classification is:
questions.exp: TT leprosy is characterized by 1–2 well-defined, fully anesthetic lesions with dry, hairless surfaces. Histopathology shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas eroding the basal layer (Grenz zone absent), SSS negative, and strong cell-mediated immunity.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with butterfly rash, joint pain, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers has ANA 1:320 and elevated anti-dsDNA. Which antibody is MOST specific for her diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm antibody has ~99% specificity for SLE, making it the most specific (though sensitivity is only 25–30%). Anti-dsDNA is also highly specific and correlates with disease activity and nephritis. Anti-histone is characteristic of drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with multiple flaccid bullae on oral mucosa and skin that rupture easily leaving raw erosions. Nikolsky sign is positive. Histopathology shows suprabasal acantholysis with a 'tombstone' basal layer. DIF shows intercellular IgG ('fishnet'). The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein 3 (Dsg3) predominantly, causing mucosal lesions. When anti-Dsg1 antibodies are also present, skin blisters occur. Suprabasal acantholysis and 'tombstone' row of basal keratinocytes, with intercellular IgG on DIF, are hallmarks.

questions.q: A 62-year-old man has a changing pigmented lesion on his back. Excision biopsy shows malignant melanoma at 1.2 mm Breslow thickness with no ulceration and no mitoses. Per AJCC 8th edition, the T category is:
questions.exp: AJCC 8th edition: T2 = 1.01–2.0 mm. T2a = no ulceration; T2b = with ulceration. At 1.2 mm without ulceration, this is T2a. T1 is ≤1.0 mm, T3 is 2.01–4.0 mm, T4 is >4 mm.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with chronic diarrhea presents with intensely pruritic vesicles on the elbows and buttocks. Histopathology shows subepidermal blisters with neutrophilic papillary microabscesses. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papillae. The associated systemic disease is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is closely associated with celiac disease. Gluten-free diet controls both. Anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA and anti-endomysial IgA are positive. Granular IgA at dermal papillae on DIF distinguishes it from linear IgA disease.

questions.q: A patient with moderate-to-severe psoriasis requires biologic therapy. Which biologic specifically targets IL-17A?
questions.exp: Secukinumab (Cosentyx) and ixekizumab are anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibodies. Bimekizumab targets IL-17A and IL-17F. Adalimumab/etanercept target TNF-α; ustekinumab targets IL-12/23 (p40 subunit); dupilumab targets IL-4Rα (IL-4/IL-13 signaling) for atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with generalized erythema, painful skin tenderness, and sheetlike peeling sparing the mucous membranes. The exfoliative toxin responsible splits the skin at which level?
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B (serine proteases) from phage group II S. aureus, which cleave desmoglein 1 in the stratum granulosum, causing a very superficial blister. Mucosa is spared (unlike TEN, which splits at the DEJ).

questions.q: A 40-year-old diabetic woman presents with vulvar pruritus, erythema, white curdy discharge, and satellite lesions. KOH preparation shows pseudohyphae and budding yeasts. First-line treatment is:
opts: Clotrimazole 1% cream / 100 mg vaginal pessary for 7 days
Terbinafine 250 mg orally daily for 2 weeks
Griseofulvin 500 mg orally daily for 4 weeks
Ketoconazole 200 mg orally daily for 2 weeks
questions.exp: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is treated with topical azoles (clotrimazole, miconazole) as first-line. Oral fluconazole 150 mg single dose is an equally effective alternative. Terbinafine and griseofulvin are active against dermatophytes, not Candida.

questions.q: A 6-year-old develops fever followed by pruritic vesicles on the trunk in different stages (macules, vesicles, pustules, and crusts simultaneously). The 'dew drop on rose petal' appearance is caused by:
questions.exp: Varicella (chickenpox) is caused by VZV. The characteristic feature is lesions in all stages of evolution simultaneously, centrifugal spread (trunk → face → extremities), and the 'dew drop on rose petal' appearance (clear vesicle on erythematous base). Treated with acyclovir if started within 24 hours.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painful, soft genital ulcer with undermined ragged edges and unilateral tender inguinal bubo. Gram stain shows small Gram-negative rods in a 'school of fish' pattern. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) presents with painful soft ulcers and tender suppurative buboes. Treatment: azithromycin 1 g single dose OR ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose OR ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD for 3 days OR erythromycin 500 mg QID for 7 days.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man with borderline tuberculoid leprosy develops sudden erythema and edema of existing skin patches with acute neuritis and loss of nerve function over 48 hours. No systemic fever or new lesions. This is:
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL). It is a delayed hypersensitivity (Type IV) reaction causing acute inflammation of existing lesions and severe neuritis without systemic features. Treated with prednisolone 40–60 mg/day tapered over 6 months to prevent permanent nerve damage.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with heliotrope rash, periorbital edema, Gottron's papules over the MCPJs, proximal muscle weakness, and elevated CK. The skin finding PATHOGNOMONIC for this condition is:
questions.exp: Gottron's papules — flat-topped violaceous papules and plaques over the knuckles (MCPJs, PIPJs, DIPJs) — are pathognomonic for dermatomyositis. Heliotrope rash is characteristic but not pathognomonic. Mechanic's hands, V-sign, and shawl sign are associated features.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on urticarial plaques on the abdomen and flexures. Nikolsky sign is negative. Histopathology shows subepidermal blisters with eosinophils. DIF reveals linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. The primary target antigen is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid targets BP180 (collagen XVII, particularly the NC16A ectodomain) and BP230. Features: tense blisters (subepidermal), negative Nikolsky, eosinophilic infiltrate, and linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF. Type VII collagen is the target in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent papule on the nose with telangiectasias and central ulceration. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels. Histopathology reveals peripheral palisading of basaloid cells with retraction artifact. The most common risk factor is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer and is predominantly caused by cumulative UV radiation exposure (especially UVB). Other risk factors include PTCH1 mutations (Gorlin syndrome), ionizing radiation, and arsenic. Arborizing blood vessels on dermoscopy and peripheral palisading on histology are characteristic.

questions.q: Wood's lamp examination is performed for a patient with vitiligo. The wavelength of UV light emitted by Wood's lamp is:
questions.exp: Wood's lamp emits long-wave UVA at approximately 365 nm. Uses include: vitiligo (chalk-white fluorescence), pityriasis versicolor (golden-yellow), erythrasma (coral-red due to porphyrins from Corynebacterium minutissimum), tinea capitis from Microsporum species (green fluorescence), and assessment of pigmentation depth.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman on long-term methotrexate for psoriasis. The most serious long-term complication and the preferred non-invasive monitoring test are:
opts: Hepatic fibrosis; serum PIIINP (procollagen type III N-terminal peptide)
Pulmonary fibrosis; chest X-ray with PFTs
Bone marrow suppression; complete blood count
questions.exp: The most serious long-term complication of methotrexate is hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis. PIIINP (procollagen III aminopeptide) is the preferred non-invasive serum marker. Liver biopsy is considered when cumulative dose exceeds 1.5 g or when PIIINP levels are persistently elevated. Folate supplementation reduces hematologic and GI side effects.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with a unilaterally swollen, hot, bright red lower leg with a raised, sharply demarcated margin, fever, and chills. The most common causative organism is:
questions.exp: Erysipelas is a superficial dermal and lymphatic infection. The sharply demarcated raised border (distinguishing it from cellulitis which has indistinct borders) is characteristic. Predominantly caused by Group A Streptococcus (S. pyogenes). Treatment: phenoxymethylpenicillin or amoxicillin orally; severe cases require IV penicillin.

questions.q: A 55-year-old diabetic man has dystrophic, thickened, yellow-brown toenails with subungual hyperkeratosis. KOH shows hyphae. Dermatophyte Test Medium turns red. The most effective oral treatment for toenail onychomycosis is:
opts: Fluconazole 150 mg once weekly for 12 months
questions.exp: Terbinafine (allylamine) has the highest mycological cure rates for dermatophyte onychomycosis (>70%). It is fungicidal and achieves high nail concentrations. Pulse itraconazole (200 mg BD for 1 week/month × 3–4 pulses) is an alternative. Griseofulvin requires much longer treatment with lower efficacy. Ketoconazole is avoided due to hepatotoxicity.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child has multiple flesh-colored, dome-shaped papules with central umbilication on the trunk. On squeezing, a white caseous material extrudes. The causative agent belongs to:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscipoxvirus, a large double-stranded DNA virus of the family Poxviridae. The squeezed material contains Henderson-Patterson bodies (intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies, visible on H&E). It is transmitted by direct contact or autoinoculation.

questions.q: A 30-year-old MSM presents with inguinal lymphadenopathy showing the pathognomonic 'groove sign.' He recalls a transient small painless genital papule 3 weeks ago. The causative serovars are:
opts: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by C. trachomatis serovars L1, L2 (most common), and L3. The 'groove sign' (adenopathy separated by Poupart's ligament) is classic but seen in only ~15–20% of cases. Treatment: doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: Which histopathological feature best distinguishes mid-borderline (BB) leprosy from borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy?
opts: Dimorphic 'punched-out' lesions with an outer sloping and inner steep edge in BB
Satellite lesions around the main plaque in BB
Well-formed epithelioid granulomas extending to the basal layer in BB
Positive slit-skin smear exclusively in BT
questions.exp: BB (mid-borderline) leprosy has dimorphic, unstable 'Swiss cheese' or 'punched-out' lesions — an outer sloping edge and inner abrupt edge. Granulomas are poorly formed with few lymphocytes. BT has satellite lesions, more defined borders, and better granuloma formation, though not as tight as TT. SSS is typically negative in TT and BT but may be weakly positive in BB.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, pitting fingertip scars, calcinosis, and telangiectasias. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive. The diagnosis is:
opts: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc / CREST syndrome)
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasias) = limited cutaneous SSc. Anti-centromere antibodies (ACA) are characteristic of lcSSc. Diffuse SSc is associated with anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) and carries worse prognosis due to rapid progression and internal organ involvement.

questions.q: A 55-year-old smoker presents with a firm, hyperkeratotic ulcerating lesion on the lower lip. Histopathology shows invasive squamous cells with keratin pearls. The most important etiological factors for lip SCC are:
opts: Chronic UV radiation and tobacco use
questions.exp: SCC of the lower lip (vermilion border) is predominantly caused by chronic actinic damage (UVB) and tobacco use (smoking/chewing). Actinic cheilitis is the precursor lesion. Lower lip SCC has higher metastatic risk than head-and-neck SCC. HPV 16/18 are more important in oropharyngeal and anogenital SCC.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with plaque psoriasis develops new psoriatic plaques exactly along a scratch mark sustained two weeks prior. This phenomenon is classified as:
questions.exp: Koebner's isomorphic phenomenon refers to the development of new skin disease lesions at sites of trauma in patients with that disease. Seen in psoriasis, lichen planus, vitiligo, and warts. Renbok (reverse Koebner) refers to the clearing of a dermatosis at a site of trauma. Pathergy occurs in Behcet's disease.

questions.q: A 38-year-old renal transplant recipient on cyclosporine for 5 years develops rapidly multiplying verrucous lesions on sun-exposed skin with histological evidence of dysplasia. The primary mechanism of cyclosporine-enhanced skin carcinogenesis is:
opts: Impaired immune surveillance with oncogenic HPV reactivation
questions.exp: Cyclosporine causes immunosuppression, leading to: (1) impaired CD8+ T-cell tumor surveillance, (2) reactivation of oncogenic HPV (particularly in beta-HPV types), and (3) direct procarcinogenic effects independent of immunity. In transplant patients, the SCC:BCC ratio reverses (SCC becomes more common), and tumors are more aggressive.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with multibacillary leprosy on dapsone monotherapy (before MDT era) develops pallor, jaundice, and methemoglobinemia after 3 weeks. The mechanism of dapsone-induced hemolysis involves:
opts: Oxidative RBC damage by hydroxylamine metabolites, exacerbated by G6PD deficiency
Autoimmune IgG-mediated hemolysis via molecular mimicry
questions.exp: Dapsone is N-hydroxylated to hydroxylamine derivatives (via CYP2C9/3A4) that generate reactive oxygen species, causing oxidative hemolysis and methemoglobinemia in all patients (dose-dependent). This is markedly exacerbated in G6PD deficiency. Baseline G6PD screening and regular CBC monitoring are essential. Cimetidine inhibits dapsone hydroxylation and can reduce methemoglobinemia.
